$comment: Client problem vocabulary (issue #1176, owner comment "De-risking dynamic composition", 2026-09-22). Advisor offers these as confirmation cards -- the client confirms a PROBLEM, never picks a package. Seeded one per role, restating that role's own jobQuestion in docs/contracts/role-loop-archetypes.json in the client's words, because no package yet declares its own foundry.solves (issue #1172, in progress on another branch). Once a role declares real solves entries, its own `problem` id there is the source of truth for scripts/lib/capability-catalogue.mjs#composeKitFromProblems; groundedInRole below only names the seed role a fallback entry was derived from and is not itself consulted at composition time. Id rule: '<role>-<two-to-four-word-slug>', chosen once and stable -- the role prefix guarantees no collision as the catalogue grows, and a rewritten `statement` is a one-line edit that never touches `id`. Do not repurpose a retired id for a different problem; add a new one instead.

problems.statement: Is this worth it for us?
We don't know if how we actually operate still matches how we say we operate.
We're not sure who can do what anymore.
We can't tell if what's running matches what we declared.
Requests come in and we lose track of what people actually asked for.
We ship fast and our own operating rules don't keep up.
We don't know if a real person would actually keep this.
Our product doesn't look or feel like it was made with care.
People ask us for things and don't hear back in time, or at all.
We put things out there and don't know if the right people respond.
We ship fast and things break.
We're not sure what's actually installed anymore, or whether it's current.
We hold data on people and can't say why, or let them see or fix it.
We don't know who holds which keys, or how we'd take one back.
Messages go out and we don't know if they actually arrived.
We can't tell what's really happening in our own systems.
We're not sure what's actually live, or that it matches what we approved.
We can't explain what we are.
Our words don't sound like us, or nobody signed off on them.
